clauses.en: Pace is the speed at which a rule changes (for the run of configuration and rule and for the reading step, see 八·十三; for its law, see 八·十四).

For any values among which two differ: the paths produced by a rule left unchanged over a fast layer (the configuration moving by this rule), read through a reading into values of at most N kinds, are such that any two that are the same over a stretch of L steps are the same throughout, exactly where L ≥ 2N − 1.

Capture through the rule is a rule read from the ratio of what it selects: in a run of configuration and rule, the rule read at a reading step does not fall as the configuration's ratio does not fall (where the ratio is not lower, the rule read is not lower, whatever the rule at that time).

If under every rule that tilts toward the carriers selection does not lower the ratio, and the rule read does not fall as the ratio does not fall: first, if the starting rule tilts toward the carriers and every rule read tilts toward them, then the ratio falls at no step, and after every reading step the run is locked (the rule tilts toward the carriers, and the rule the ratio reads is not below this rule).

Second, if every rule not below a rule that tilts toward the carriers also tilts toward them, then from a locked configuration the run is locked at every step after, and neither the ratio nor the rule falls;

if from a locked configuration the rule is replaced by any rule that still tilts toward the carriers, then after every reading step the rule is not below that of the run without the replacement, and the run is locked again.
Third, if every rule read tilts toward the carriers, then every path, whatever its start, is locked from after the second reading step on;
this bound is exact.
Closed capture is where the reading of the rule is itself made by the ratio.

Wherever the configuration of the fast layer is a pair of the ratio and what lies beyond the ratio, and neither the next ratio nor the rule read reads what lies beyond the ratio: any two histories whose ratio and rule start the same have the same ratio and the same rule at every step, whatever lies beyond the ratio.

If further what lies beyond the ratio grows by at least one at every step, and the run starts from a locked configuration under the condition of the second part of 十一·二十三: then at step t what lies beyond the ratio is no less than its start plus t, while the path is locked at every step and neither the ratio nor the rule is below its start.

Wherever the reading of the rule at reading steps is made by the ratio (not falling as the ratio does not fall), and the rule is read off from this reading and the ratio (not falling as the two do not fall): the rule together with its reading is one rule, read from the ratio;
if it is locked under the condition of the second part of 十一·二十三, then none of the ratio, the rule and the reading falls;

if from a locked configuration the rule is replaced by any rule that still tilts toward the carriers and the reading by any reading (higher or lower), then after every reading step neither the rule nor the reading is below that of the run without the replacement, and the run is locked again;
if the rule read tilts toward the carriers at every reading and every ratio, then every path, whatever its start, is locked from after the second reading step on.
Reading (AI, D26, D45): coupling beyond support is the couplings joined to a selection reaching what admission does not mark.
Its routes are three: a condition coupling in by its level, admitted histories, and the couplings of others used together.

title_en: The three routes of coupling beyond support

clauses.en: The routes of coupling beyond support: first, a condition coupling in by its level: where the sameness or difference of conditions is decided, for every condition that couples into a formation by its level, if the level of this condition is raised at every step by one and the same positive amount, then at every step the levels of the original web and of the raised web are not alike through this formation's couplings.
Second, admitted histories: for their testing and their error, see 九·十四.
Third, the couplings of others used together: for its laws, see 十一·二十七 to 十一·三十一.
Pooled coupling is the couplings of the members of a region used together.
Selection through pooled coupling is a selection that is the same on any two histories that are alike through each member's couplings up to a given step.
What pooling adds is what pooled coupling adds;
pooled as one member is pooled coupling equal to the couplings of one member.
Every selection through pooled coupling up to a step is the same on two histories exactly where the two are alike through every member's couplings;
some selection through pooled coupling holds of the one and does not hold of the other exactly where not every member finds them alike.
Where one member separates them through its couplings, some selection through its couplings is also a selection through pooled coupling and separates them.
If a family lists all the members and each member's being alike is decided, then pooled coupling separates them exactly where some member separates them.

The selections through pooled coupling are exactly the selections through one member's couplings exactly where every two histories alike through this member's couplings are alike through every member's (pooled as one member);

if two histories are alike through this member's couplings and not alike through every member's, then some selection through pooled coupling is not a selection through this member's couplings (what pooling adds).

title_en: The coupling closure of a region; reading another's couplings

clauses.en: The coupling closure of a region is the union of the coupling closures of its members.

Wherever every condition coupled into by what lies in this region's coupling closure balances at every step, and every member of the part lies outside this region's coupling closure: then for any region whose members all lie in this region's coupling closure (this region included), every selection through its pooled coupling is the same on the history of levels and on the history of levels with this part withheld.

Reading another's couplings is a formation coupled in addition, by level, into every condition the other is coupled into (by threshold or by level): every selection through the pooled coupling of the two is a selection through the couplings of the formation that reads so;
if the other has taking and giving at some condition that couples into it, then the coupling closure of the formation that reads so is exactly the coupling closure of the region the two form.

If in two flows the others all follow one law of taking and giving that reads through couplings, both flows balance, what takes part is the same, the starting levels are the same, and the part's moves are alike within the coupling closure that each member of a region has through the two flows: then for any region whose members all lie in this region's coupling closure through the two flows (also where the part is this region), every selection through its pooled coupling is the same on the level histories of the two flows;
every formation that separates the two flows through its couplings up to some step lies outside this region's coupling closure.
If a move changes a formation's admission at some step, then this formation lies outside this region's coupling closure;

its admission at this step is a selection through pooled coupling, from this step on, of every region that contains this formation, and is not a selection, at any step, of any region whose members all lie in this region's coupling closure.

Wherever the level history of the later flow widens that of the earlier flow, there is a formation admitted at some step by the later flow's levels and not by the earlier flow's, and its admission is likewise so.

Wherever a law of taking and giving reads, for every formation outside the part, through its couplings, and the members of a region all lie outside the part: every selection through the moves of this region's members (under this law) is a selection through pooled coupling;
if a family lists all the members, each member's being alike is decided, and the moves of this region separate two histories, then some member separates them through its couplings.

Wherever, for each formation, each step and each history, being alike through couplings with a given history is decided, there is some condition, and the members all lie outside the part: across a step, the members' taking and giving at every condition is alike under every law that reads through couplings, exactly where the members are alike through couplings up to this step.
Under the conditions of 十一·三十, every formation in this region's coupling closure and outside the part takes and gives alike in the two flows at every step and every condition.
Some member of this region lies in the part's responsive reach exactly where some member of the part lies in this region's coupling closure through the two flows.
Coupling strength is the multiple by which, as a taking and giving varies with a condition's level, the gap in what it takes and gives is bounded by the gap in this level.
The carried amount is the level history that the law of carrying gives, step by step, from the coupling strengths, the starting gap and the part's gap.

Wherever a family lists every condition, each once: for every law that reads only what is already fixed and any two flows under this law, where both flows balance, what takes part is the same, the relata outside the part follow this law with coupling strength at most k, what the part does differs by at most σ, and the starting levels differ by at most δ: for all such, the gap at a condition at a step is at most a, exactly where its carried amount is at most a.
The carried amount is positive exactly where there is a path along the steps that reaches it from the starting gap, the part's gap and positive coupling strengths.
A loop is a chain of couplings from a condition back to this condition.
Wherever every coupling is present at every step: from every starting gap, some expansion order equals the carried amount at c at every step, exactly where no condition upstream of c lies on a loop.
Closing is where the coupling of a step joins the head and the tail of a chain, and a loop first exists.
Every loop comes to be by some step.

Every loop formed by step T+1 either was already formed by step T or passes through a coupling acting at step T that reads the level of d and has taking and giving with c, with a chain from c to a condition on the loop and a chain from this condition to d.
When a taking and giving first responds to the level of the condition it gives to, a loop of one condition is formed.

title_en: Loops lie within what is read, and their forming cannot be seen in advance

clauses.en: If no relatum outside the part reads the level of c at any step, then among the couplings restricted to what is read no loop passes through c, and downstream of c there is only c.

Wherever a family lists every condition, the part gives no further gap after the start, the starting gap is at most D, the sum of the coupling strengths into each condition at each step is at most M, and no loop formed by step T is upstream of c: then at every step up to T the carried amount at c is at most D times a polynomial in the number of steps, of degree the number of conditions less one, whatever the couplings after.
There is a loop of a condition on itself formed at step T: at every step up to T its carried amount is the starting gap, and at every step after it doubles;
a loop of the condition on itself formed at any step after T gives, at every step up to T, a carried amount equal to it.
The filling threshold is where a level rises to a threshold and then a new coupling forms.

title_en: Coupling recurs, and what a cut loses

clauses.en: A coupling recurs where the level of d coupling into c recurs.
What a cut loses is what the carried amount, cut at an expansion order, leaves uncounted.

For every cut at expansion order j, the carried amount equals the amount at order j plus what is carried from the carried amount itself through j+1 responses in turn: what the cut loses is the latter term, however the coupling strengths go step by step.

If the gap has reached a loop, every coupling on the loop recurs, and there is a chain of recurring couplings from the loop to c: then a cut at every expansion order loses something at c at some step.
If no coupling reads the levels of step N and after, then a cut at expansion order N loses nothing, at every step, at every condition and from every starting gap.
The carried amount of the expansion orders is the sum over the paths traced back along the steps: up to a step, the sum over the paths of length j+1 is the carried amount of order j;
a cut at an expansion order is a cut of this sum.
Runaway is the carried amount growing with the steps beyond every polynomial.

Wherever the coupling strengths are the same at every step and read only the levels of the present step, what takes part is the same at every step, a family lists every condition, and the part gives no further gap after the start: the carried amount at c is bounded by a polynomial from every starting gap exactly where there is no loop upstream of c;
where the coupling strengths on a loop are all positive, the carried amount at a condition on the loop at least doubles with every loop turn.

If the part gives no further gap after the start, the starting gap is at most D, the sum of the coupling strengths into each condition at each step is at most M, and the couplings that read the levels of step N and after have no loop upstream of c: then, however the coupling strengths go step by step, the carried amount at c is bounded by a polynomial.
Frequency is the number of steps at which a coupling acts.

If the part gives no further gap after the start, the starting gap is at most D, the sum of the coupling strengths into each condition at each step is at most M, and the sum of the coupling strengths into each condition is zero at unmarked steps: then the carried amount at step t is at most D times 1+M to the power a, where a is the number of marked steps before t.
If the gap has reached e and comes back from e to e through a chain along the steps, then after this round trip the carried amount at e is at least twice what it was before the round trip.

If the carried amount at e is positive at some step and round trips follow one another after it: if for every polynomial there is some i such that 2 to the power i exceeds the value of this polynomial at the step of the i-th round trip, then the carried amount at e runs away.
There is a loop whose coupling recurs and that does not run away.

The return map is the composition of what the loop links do in turn: a gap is sent into the first loop link, each loop link hands what it receives on to the next, and what the last loop link hands back is the return map.
If every loop link hands on no less than it receives, then the gap at every loop turn is no smaller than at the start;
if the gap at some loop turn is smaller than at the start, then some loop link hands on, at some gap, less than it receives.
If the return map is zero at zero and less than every positive gap at that gap, then a gap d is zero by the d-th loop turn and zero at every loop turn after;
this bound is exact.
If every loop link hands on exactly what it receives, then the gap at every loop turn is as at the start.

If a loop has loop links and every loop link hands on at least twice what it receives, then after n loop turns the gap is at least 2 to the power n times its start, and from a positive gap it passes every bound.
Wherever every loop link of a loop multiplies by a whole-number factor: if the product of the factors is zero, then from the first loop turn on the gap is zero at every loop turn;
if it is one, then the gap at every loop turn is as at the start;
if it is no less than two, then from a positive gap the gap passes every bound.
So the gap at every loop turn is either zero or no smaller than at the loop turn before;
where the gap at some loop turn is positive and less than at the loop turn before (falling gradually), the loop has a loop link that is not a multiplication.

If a loop link hands back zero and the loop links after it hand on nothing when they receive nothing, then after the first loop turn the gap is zero at every loop turn, whatever the loop links before it.

If a loop link after it hands on something when it receives nothing, the gap can be positive again: there is a loop in which the loop link handing back zero is followed by a loop link that adds one, and after the first loop turn the gap is one at every loop turn, whatever its start.
Feedback is where the gap between two histories at a condition is, after every step, the return map of the gap before it.
Wherever two flows balance at c at every step: their taking and giving responds to their gap by f from step s on, exactly where the gap at every step after s is f of the gap before it;
so the gap at step s+n is the value of f after n loop turns run from the gap at step s, one loop turn per step.
The break is where the level of c falls below the threshold and the law turns from not reading it to reading it.

Wherever the law reads c only below the threshold: if both flows balance and what takes part is the same, what the part does is the same, what lies outside the part follows this law, the start differs only at c with the latter higher by d, and c in the former is not below its threshold at any step before T: then up to T the levels of every condition other than c are equal in the two flows, and c in the latter is higher by d at every step.

If the law also reads only what is already fixed, and c is the only one marked: at a step up to which c is not below the threshold at any step, what the law gives is the same as its pre-break law (the law that reads c, where it is below the threshold, as if it were at its threshold);
the pre-break law has coupling strength zero at c; among the couplings restricted to what is read no loop passes through c, and downstream of c there is only c.
Unread before the break is where what is coupled into before the break does not bound how near or far the break is.

Wherever c does not couple into formation g by its level, and the sameness or difference of conditions is decided: for any step u, if at every step up to u every dependence of g other than at c is met, then there is a web, differing only in that the level of c is raised by one and the same number at every step, that admits g at every step up to u, and at every step at which the original web admits g the levels of the two webs are alike through g's couplings.

Wherever the sameness or difference of formations is decided, g's taking and giving goes through its couplings, the others' taking and giving at the conditions coupling into g is the same in both flows, what takes part is the same in both flows, every condition coupling into g balances in both flows, and at the start what couples into g is no less in the latter and what couples into g by its level is equal in the two flows: if the gap at some condition coupling into g changes by some step, then it is not the case that the original web admits g at every step before.

Without overshoot is where, at a step, in the joint taking and giving at c, the joint taking exceeds the joint giving by no more than the level exceeds m, and the joint giving exceeds the joint taking by no more than the level falls short of m.
Wherever a flow balances at c at a step: it is without overshoot exactly where the level at the next step lies between m and the level at this step (on the same side as this step, not farther).
If a flow balances at c and is without overshoot for n steps, then the level after n steps lies between m and the starting level.

Two-sided regulation is where the joint taking and giving at c opposes the departure on both sides of m and is without overshoot: above m the joint taking exceeds the joint giving, and below m the joint giving exceeds the joint taking.
If a flow balances and is in two-sided regulation at m at every step from T on: then at a step at which the level is not at m, its gap from m falls by at least one;
the gap after n steps is at most the first gap less n;
by the step T plus the first gap the level is m, and it is m at every step after.
Starting below m, it is at m by the step T plus the amount by which it falls short of m, and does not move from it.
Overshoot is an opposing joint taking and giving that exceeds the gap between its level and m.
If a flow balances at c at a step, and the joint taking and giving opposes the departure and is not without overshoot: if the level is above m, then the level at the next step is below m;
if it is below m, then the level at the next step is above m.
There is a flow that balances at every step, opposes the departure on both sides and overshoots at every step, is above m at even steps and below m at odd steps, and never reaches m.
One-sided response is responding on one side only.

There is a flow that satisfies the premise of the law of rising to m, is without overshoot at every step, is above m without opposing, and is above m at every step: one-sided response is not two-sided regulation.
Reading late is a response function reading ℓ steps late: what it gives and takes at a step is fixed only by what the rest of the whole did ℓ+1 steps or more before.

If a response function reads ℓ steps late and, from a starting configuration, for every rest of the whole that moves the level by at most d at each step, its level history lies between a and b at every step, with 0<a: then a plus 2(ℓ+1)d is at most b.

There is a response function that at each step offsets what the rest of the whole moved ℓ+1 steps before, and neither takes nor gives in the first ℓ+1 steps: it reads ℓ steps late, and from a starting configuration not below (ℓ+1)d, for every such rest of the whole, its level history lies at every step within (ℓ+1)d above or below the starting configuration: the width of this region is exact.
The relay is: reading its level, it gives M where the level is below a, takes M where it is above b, and neither takes nor gives where it is between a and b.

Wherever a is at most b, 0<a, 0<M, and (ℓ+1)M is at most b+1: every flow whose joint taking and giving at c is only the relay reading ℓ steps late and that balances at every step, from any starting configuration whose level in the first ℓ+1 steps is one and the same number below a, lies between a and b at every step from some step on, exactly where a+(ℓ+1)M is at most b+1.
Descent: where g takes part across a step and gives to x, and x comes to stand across this step, x descends from g, and g is what x descends from.
If a relatum comes to stand across a step and balances across this step, then there is something it descends from at this step.
If a flow balances and only the active give, and an embodied relatum arises across a step, then there is another relatum that is active at that step and is what it descends from.
There are a flow and a web in which a relatum descends from something, its arising is at a step after its coming to stand, and nothing is given to it when it arises;
there are a flow and a web that are unceasing and in which no relatum descends from anything.
Inheritance is where, at the step at which x descends from g, what x depends on after the step g also depends on at the step of giving.
Inheritance covers two: the dependences x newly forms across this step, and those x already had that it still has after the step.
If x does not depend on c at the step of giving, then x has inheritance at c exactly where, if x forms a dependence on c across this step, g depends on c at the step of giving.

If a relatum comes to stand across a step, balances across this step, and has inheritance at c from everything it descends from at this step: then, if it depends on c after the step, something it descends from also depends on c at the step of giving;
if nothing taking part at this step depends on c, then it does not depend on c after the step.

Transmission is inheritance with a bound on need: for a condition c and a bound δ, wherever x descends from g and x depends on c after the step, g depends on c at the step of giving, and the need of x on c is at most the need of g on c plus δ.
Transmission is exactly inheritance and the bound on need together.

If the flow balances, then transmission implies transmission from some giver: everything that comes to stand and depends on c has something it descends from that depends on c at the step of giving, with its need at most that one's need plus δ.

The latter is strictly weaker than transmission: there are a flow and a web that balance, in which only the active give, that are dependent, where transmission from some giver holds and transmission holds for no δ.

If a world is dependent, balances, has only the active giving, has only the active taking and taking only from what they draw from, dissipates, is embodied, and has a census (the seven suppositions other than transmission), and some offspring in it depends on something after its step, then removing one dependence, at the step of giving, of something it descends from yields a world that has these seven suppositions and in which transmission does not hold.
For every property of worlds that does not change when one dependence is removed and that implies transmission, no world with this property has an offspring that depends on something after its step.

The reading that what an offspring depends on when it first comes to stand is only what the things it descends from draw from at the step of giving, together with drawing implying dependence, implies inheritance;
for finite worlds with these seven suppositions, with either of the two missing, inheritance does not follow.
For every finite world that balances, dissipates, is embodied and is dependent, transmission holds exactly where there is inheritance at every condition.

title_en: The eight suppositions do not follow from one another

clauses.en: The eight suppositions of a world: dependent (二·五), balance (一·十五), only the active give, only the active take and take only from what they draw from (一·十六), dissipation (四·四), embodied (二·十一), census (三·六), transmission (十三·三).
For the first six suppositions and for reserve (二·十), each has a world that satisfies it and a world that does not;
the eight suppositions do not follow from one another: for each supposition there is a world that satisfies the other seven and not it.
The world read off the path that a law of taking and giving produces, with the rest of the whole counted, has all of the first four suppositions (一·十七, 二·五).
For every world with the rest of the whole counted: if the members of the family taking part at each step are distinct and each step is closed on a given family, then it has a census;
the world with the rest of the whole counted is embodied exactly where the original world balances and each relatum takes and gives exactly at the steps at which its level is positive.
For a world read off a law that reads only what is already fixed, with the rest of the whole counted, the rest of the whole is never active exactly where its path is feasible.

Dissipation, embodiment and transmission are properties of the law of taking and giving: among worlds read off a law of taking and giving, with the rest of the whole counted, the rest of the whole never active, and the first four suppositions all holding, for each of these three suppositions some satisfy it and some do not.
Evolution is where only what is admitted has offspring, and the needs passed on within the bound are selected within the bound.
Wherever only the active give and the web is dependent: at the step at which x descends from g, g is admitted;
what is not admitted at a step has no offspring at this step;
what is never admitted never has offspring.
If moreover c is transmitted within δ, then wherever x descends from g and depends on c after the step, the need of x on c is at most the level of c at the step of giving plus δ.

If the flow also balances, then wherever x descends from g at step S＋n and depends on c after the step, the need of x plus what is taken from c in the n steps from step S is at most the level of c at S plus what is given to c in these n steps plus δ.
Variation is the rise and fall of an offspring's amount against the amount of what it descends from.

For every family in which each member has its family of offspring, with the amounts of members and offspring read in any way as natural numbers: the total of the offspring's amounts plus all the falls equals the total of the members' amounts, each counted by its number of offspring, plus all the rises (the account of variation).
If every member has k offspring, then the total counted by offspring is k times the total of the members' amounts.

For every family, with the members' weightings and amounts read in any way as natural numbers: the number of members times the total of the products of each member's weighting and amount, plus the discordance, equals the total of the weightings times the total of the amounts, plus the concordance.
The selection term is the concordance less the discordance, with the number of offspring as the weighting.

With the number of offspring as the weighting: the number of members times the total counted by offspring exceeds the total number of offspring times the total of the members' amounts exactly where the concordance exceeds the discordance;
the two are equal exactly where the concordance and the discordance are equal.

Joined with the account of variation: the number of members times the total of the offspring's amounts, plus the number of members times the falls, plus the discordance, equals the total number of offspring times the total of the members' amounts, plus the concordance, plus the number of members times the rises.

title_en: The family mean across successive families

clauses.en: Successive family: the first is a family, each member of each successive family has its family of offspring, and the next successive family is the offspring of the members.

The family mean is compared by cross-multiplying: it does not change across a step exactly where the number of members of this successive family times the falls, plus the discordance, equals the concordance plus the number of members of this successive family times the rises;
it rises exactly where the former is less than the latter.
If the family mean of a successive family differs from that of the first, then at some step before it the two sides do not offset each other, and checking step by step finds it;
if there is exact transmission at every step (each offspring's amount equals its member's amount), then at some step before it the discordance differs from the concordance;
if at every step every member has the same number of offspring, then at some step before it the falls differ from the rises.

title_en: What is admitted is not selected against

clauses.en: Wherever only the active give and the web is dependent, and the offspring listed for the members of a family all descend from their member at this step: if an amount at every admitted member is not below the amounts of all the members, then the discordance is zero and the selection term is not negative.

In this flow, wherever the successive families are all formed by descent and an amount at the admitted members of each successive family is not below the amounts of all members of that successive family: if the falls at every step of a stretch are zero, then the family mean does not fall over this stretch;
if there is exact transmission at every step of this stretch and the family mean changes, then the change is a rise, and at some step the concordance exceeds the discordance.

title_en: Selection on the number of offspring

clauses.en: A weighting read against itself has no discordance: the number of members times the total of the squares of the weightings equals the square of the total of the weightings plus the concordance (the total of the squares of the pairwise gaps);
so it is not below the square of the total of the weightings, and is equal to it exactly where the weightings are all the same.

With the number of offspring as the weighting: the number of members times the total of the numbers of offspring counted by offspring is not below the square of the total number of offspring, and is equal to it exactly where every member has the same number of offspring.
Reading successive families with the number of offspring as the amount: if the falls at a step are zero, then the family mean of the number of offspring does not fall across this step;

if there is exact transmission at this step, then the family mean of the number of offspring rises exactly where the concordance is positive, and does not change exactly where every member has the same number of offspring.

For every family, with weightings and amounts read in any way as natural numbers: the square of the concordance plus the discordance is at most the total of the squared pairwise gaps of the weightings times the total of the squared pairwise gaps of the amounts;
where the amount is the weighting itself, the two are equal.

If there is exact transmission at some step of successive families, then the square of the rise or fall of the family mean (by cross-multiplying) is at most the total of the squared pairwise gaps of the numbers of offspring times the total of the squared pairwise gaps of this amount.

title_en: The bound on the number of offspring

clauses.en: Where a member's offspring at a step all descend from it, their number is at most the total it gives to the offspring at this step.

Where a family balances and dissipates across a step: if the offspring are distinct and are all members of the family, their number plus the number of takers that take from the family at this step is at most the family's total level before this step.

If the successive families are all formed by descent, the offspring are all members of one family, and this family balances and dissipates at every step from the first step to the step numbered by its starting total level, then the successive family numbered by the starting total level plus one is empty (the first successive family is numbered zero);

read with the number of offspring as the amount, if the next successive family has members, then at some step before the step of the starting total level the number of members times the falls exceeds the concordance plus the number of members times the rises.

Where a family is listed group by group as k groups with the same number of members in each: the concordance of the whole family, plus k times the within-group discordance, plus the among-group discordance, equals the discordance of the whole family, plus k times the within-group concordance, plus the among-group concordance.

So, for an amount whose within-group concordance is not more than its within-group discordance, the concordance of the whole family exceeds its discordance only where the among-group concordance exceeds the among-group discordance.

Where the groups differ in their numbers of members, taking a common multiple of the groups' numbers of members, counting each group's own terms by its multiplier, and reading the among-group terms member by member from the groups' family means, there is also a corresponding decomposition (each term multiplied by a multiplier the common multiple fixes);

if a successive family has members, is listed group by group as groups with the same family means, and has exact transmission, then its family mean rises exactly where the within-group concordance (counted so) exceeds the discordance.

title_en: Selection among groups by having no offspring

clauses.en: Where the groups have the same number of members and every group whose total of an amount is less than another group's has no offspring, there is no among-group discordance;
so the selection term of the whole family is positive exactly where k times the within-group discordance is less than k times the within-group concordance plus the among-group concordance;
if moreover this amount is the same within each group, then the selection term of the whole family is not negative.

In a flow: where the flow balances, only the active give, the web is dependent, and for a condition c every renewer of c depends on it with need not below m, if at each of the n steps from T what is given to c is less than what is taken from c, and the level of c at T is less than n plus m, then from T＋n on nothing that depends on c at its step with need not below m has offspring.
Where only the active give and the successive families are formed by descent, if no member of a successive family is active, then the next successive family is empty.

Where the first successive family is listed group by group, the members of each group all have, for an amount, the value with which their group was first set, and there is exact transmission at every step: then in the groups formed by descent every member, across the successive families, carries the first value of its group, and there is no within-group selection term;

where every group formed by descent has members in the t-th successive family, the family mean rises from the t-th successive family to the next exactly where, read by a common multiple of their numbers of members, the concordance of the groups' family means with the numbers of offspring exceeds the discordance.

In a flow: where only the active give and the successive families are formed by descent, if in every successive family before the T-th, for every group whose first value is less than another group's, the members of what is formed by descent from it are all inactive, then the family mean of the T-th successive family is not below that of the first;

if in the t-th successive family, for every group whose first value is less than another group's, the members of what is formed by descent from it are all inactive, while in what is formed by descent from a group with a larger first value some member leaves offspring, and beside it what is formed by descent from a group with a smaller first value has members, then the family mean rises from the t-th successive family to the next.

Under a representation in which the next successive family is not the family of offspring itself but is formed from the family of offspring by n draws with replacement: the family has p of the first kind and q of the second, and each sample has as its weight the number of ways of drawing it.
p＋q times the total, over the samples counted by their weights, of the number of first-kind draws equals n·p·(p＋q)ⁿ.

If (p＋q)·h＋g＝N·p, then the total weight of the samples whose number of first-kind draws times N is at most h times n, multiplied by n²·g², is at most N²·n·p·q·(p＋q)ⁿ, and that total weight is no less than qⁿ.

For a family of N members with h of the first kind (h at most N), each successive family drawn N times with replacement from the one before by the numbers of its kinds alone: over the histories of k successive families (each with the number of ways of drawing it as its weight), the total, counted by weight, of the number of the first kind in the last successive family equals h·(N^N)^k.
Starting with none of the first kind, every history has none at every successive family;
starting with all of the first kind, every history has all at every successive family.
If r＋2＝N^N, then the total weight of the histories that still have both kinds after k successive families is at most r^k;
the total weight of the histories fixed at the first kind, times N, is at most h·(N^N)^k, and with N·r^k added it is no less than h·(N^N)^k.
The model a selection goes through (一·三) assigns a value to each selectable.
A selection through a model, when the values of two selectables are swapped, swaps what it selects.
Wherever the sameness or difference of selectables is decided: two selectables are selected alike by every selection through a model exactly where the model assigns them the same value;
a selectable can be selected by a selection through a model that selects at most one under each model exactly where the values of the other selectables all differ from its value.
If a claim holds of one and not of the other of two selectables to which the model assigns the same value, then no selection through this model selects exactly those of which it holds.
Learning through response is learning through others' actual responses.
In the represented pair of learning through response (the learning side receives only the actual responses of the side learned from;

what is installed, the grammar, a family of questions and the levels are all given), where the side learned from has something installed, what the learning side learns from it is the same as what it learns from a side learned from that has only this installed and the same levels (the learning side's levels, components and family of questions being the same).
Where there is no response, the learning side adds no sample;
after a family of questions, the total of the two sides' levels and the amounts already used does not change.
A collective is formations that lie together in a system closure.
If there is a condition such that every formation either depends on it at some step or has taking and giving at it, then every formation lies in the system closure of every formation.
Mutual dependence is where every formation lies in the influence closure of every formation: each formation can be influenced, through a chain, by every other.
Mutual dependence holds exactly where every formation lies in the reach closure of every formation.
A common condition is a condition that every formation depends on at some step and also has taking and giving at.
If a flow has a common condition, then every formation lies in the reach closure of every formation, and the formations are in mutual dependence.
Mutual feeding is where every formation lies in the feeding closure of every formation.
Mutual feeding implies mutual dependence;
where there is mutual dependence, every formation lies in the system closure of every formation.
There is a flow in which every formation lies in the system closure of every formation and there is no mutual dependence;
there is a flow that balances and has mutual dependence, with two formations neither of which lies in the other's feeding closure.

From 十二·八 (every step marked) and 十二·七 (at least doubling with every loop turn): if the part gives no further gap after the start, the starting gap is at most D, and the sum of the coupling strengths into each condition at each step is at most M, then the carried amount at step t is at most D times 1＋M to the power t;

if moreover the couplings of a loop are present at every step (the loop of length m＋1), then after R loop turns from step T (up to step T＋(m＋1)R) the carried amount at the condition where the loop lies is at least 2 to the power R times its carried amount at step T.

Wherever the flow balances, nothing is given to a condition c for n steps from step T, and the joint taking at c at each step exceeds the sum of the joint taking at c from step T up to before it: then at each of these n steps the level of c exceeds half the level at step T, and the level at step T is no less than 2 to the power n less one.

Under taking within giving (四·十九): wherever the flow balances, there is taking within giving at a condition at every step, and every formation depends only on this condition with need at most the level of this condition at step zero, every formation is admitted at every step.
Waiting with memory is where a relatum gives at the next step exactly where it gives at this step and everything it waits on gives at this step.
Under the law of waiting with memory: if a relatum does not give at some step, then it does not give at any step after;
if a relatum does not give at the start and a chain of waiting of length k leads from it to another relatum, then the other does not give at any step from step k on;
if every relatum lies within d waitings of one relatum and this relatum does not give at the start, then from step d on no relatum gives.
Waiting without memory is where a relatum gives at the next step exactly where everything it waits on gives at this step.
Under the law of waiting without memory: if there is no chain of waiting of length L between any relata, then, whatever the start, every relatum gives at every step from step L on;
if there is a chain of waiting of length p from b back to b and b does not give at the start, then b does not give at any step that is a multiple of p.
Under the law of waiting with memory and under the law of waiting without memory, if more is waited on, then the relata giving at each step are among those that gave at the same step before.
Tolerance is where a relatum still gives when no more than tol of what it waits on are missing, with tol at least one.

Under the law of still giving while no more than tol are missing: if the members of a region all give at the start and each member waits on no more than its tol outside the region, then, whatever the other relata, the members of this region give at every step;
if everything outside a region gives at the start and each relatum waits on no more than its tol inside this region, then from step one on every relatum gives at every step;
if no relatum has a tol no less than the number it waits on, then once no relatum gives at a step, the same holds at every step after.
The law with tol zero has the same path as the law of waiting without memory.
Restoring from every start is where a relatum gives at some step from every starting configuration.

Wherever a law keeps inclusion (if the relata giving in one configuration are all among those giving in another, then the same holds at the next step): a relatum gives at step n from every starting configuration exactly where it gives at step n starting from the configuration in which none gives;
starting from the configuration in which none gives, if a relatum gives at some step, then it also gives at the next step;
what gives at step n from every starting configuration gives at every step after from every starting configuration;
if no relatum gives at the step after the configuration in which none gives, then, starting from the configuration in which none gives, no relatum gives at any step.
Giving first is where a relatum gives after every step, without regard to what it waits on.
Under the law of giving first (after every step, the relata that give first all give;

any other relatum gives at the next step if everything it waits on gives at this step), where whether each relatum gives first is decided: a relatum gives at step n from every starting configuration exactly where no chain of waiting of length n, with no relatum giving first except at its starting point, leads into it;

if there is a chain of waiting from b back to b (of positive length) with no relatum giving first except at its starting point, then, starting from the configuration in which none gives, b gives at no step;
if a relatum gives at step n from every starting configuration under the law of waiting without memory, then the same holds under the law of giving first.
A loop returning less is a loop on which a loop link hands back less than it receives.
For the steps at which the run of the return map falls and the steps at which it is zero, see 十二·九.
A race at a shared condition is where formations have joint excess at a condition over consecutive steps;
for the fall of its level and the ending of what depends on it, see 四·十九 and 四·二十.
Relative position is the position of a part's amount, counted as many times as there are parts in its family, against the sum of the amounts of the parts of its family.
For every finite family and every reading of amounts: the sum of the relative positions of the parts is zero.
Wherever the parts' amounts go from these to those: the sum of the rise counts over the whole family equals the sum of the fall counts;
a part's rise count plus the sum of the other parts' rise counts equals its fall count plus the sum of the other parts' fall counts;
if the family is not empty, then the relative positions of the parts do not all rise;
if a part's relative position rises, some other part's relative position falls.

title_en: Where a race at a shared condition ends

clauses.en: If at a condition, for n consecutive steps from step T, the flow balances and there is joint excess, a part depends on it at step T＋n, the level at step T is less than n plus its need at step T＋n, and this part is dependent at its step (active only where admitted): then this part is not active at step T＋n, whatever its relative position.

If moreover the conditions of 四·二十 all hold (balance, only the active give, dependent, every renewer depends on it with need not below m, the level at step T less than n plus m), then for every family and every reading of amounts: from step T to step T＋n the sum of the parts' rise counts equals the sum of their fall counts;
the level falls by at least n;
from step T＋n on it is below m at every step;
after this, the members of the family whose amount none exceeds, where they depend on this condition at their step with need not below m, are all inactive.

If the family is not empty and its members all depend on this condition with need not below m from step T＋n on, then at every step after there is a member of the family whose amount none exceeds, and all such members are inactive.

A relatum makes a difference where a move at a configuration breaks a dependence and, with the relatum withheld, the same move can still be taken at the configuration with it withheld, and every outcome of it keeps this dependence.
If a move breaks a dependence and, with any one relatum withheld, the same move still breaks it, then no relatum makes a difference.

If a move breaks a dependence, with a relatum withheld the same move can still be taken, and this dependence is still present and met at the configuration with it withheld, then this relatum makes a difference exactly where, after it is withheld, the same move no longer breaks the dependence.

title_en: Making a difference together, and difference made only together

clauses.en: A family makes a difference together where a move at a configuration breaks a dependence and, with the members of the family withheld together, the same move can still be taken at the configuration with them withheld together, and every outcome of it keeps this dependence.
Difference made only together is where the family makes a difference together and no member of the family makes a difference.
Wherever there is difference made only together, the family has no fewer than two members.

For every law (a move at a configuration having at most one outcome), where with each member of the family withheld the same move can be taken and this dependence is present and met at the configuration with it withheld: there is difference made only together exactly where the family makes a difference together and, with any one member withheld, the same move still breaks this dependence.
A joint plan is a finite nesting of leaves in pairs.
A configuration realizes a joint plan exactly where there are two parts that, with this configuration, satisfy the given three-place relation J, and each realizes one side of it, down to the leaves;
a leaf is read at its part.

For every lumping: if, of two configurations the lumping makes the same, one has two parts under J, then the other also has two parts under J, each the same under the lumping as the corresponding one of the first two;

if reading a leaf through the lumping is the same as reading it at the configuration: then a configuration's class realizes a joint plan under the J read through the lumping exactly where this configuration realizes it.
Exclusive footprints is where the footprint of each part lies within the footprint of what it is divided from, and two parts divided from one and the same have nothing in common in their footprints.

Wherever footprints are exclusive and a configuration realizes a joint plan (each leaf carrying a family whose members are distinct and all lie within its part's footprint): then the leaves' families, joined in order, have distinct members, all within this configuration's footprint.
Kept together is where from a configuration there is a run that lies within the regions at every step.
For every process and every configuration: from this configuration no run leaves the configurations both regions contain, exactly where no run leaves the first and no run leaves the second.
If two regions are kept together at a configuration, then from this configuration each of the two regions has a run that does not leave it.
There are a process and a configuration from which each of two regions has a run that does not leave it, and the two regions are not kept together;
for this process there is no function that, at every configuration, fixes whether the two regions are kept together from whether each of the two regions has a run that does not leave it.
A standpoint is where an evaluation starts from.
The center is the relatum where a standpoint is.
Own region is the region of a standpoint itself: the claims belonging to this standpoint.
The boundary of a self is a region that contains the center and that nothing along a given relation leads out of.
For every relation and every relatum: the region of this relatum along this relation is a boundary of a self, and every boundary of a self contains this region;
the whole of the unfolding is a boundary of a self;
where every relatum lies within this relatum's region along this relation, the whole of the unfolding is its only boundary of a self.
Taking the relata as standpoints and own region as a relatum's region along this relation, own region is the least boundary of a self.
Significance is the one given parameter of evaluation: for a standpoint, a step and a relatum, it says whether, from this standpoint, the continuation of this relatum at this step has significance.
Significance distinguishes only having from not having.
Retains is where, from a standpoint, this level history admits every continuation with significance that that history admits.
Adds is where, from a standpoint, this history admits a continuation with significance that that history does not admit.
For every significance, retains is reflexive and transitive;
if this retains with respect to that, then that does not add with respect to this;
includes implies retains, and adds implies exceeds.

title_en: Retains and adds are bounded by the margin

clauses.en: For every flow and web and any part taken, the level history with this part withheld exists;

from a standpoint, where the conditions of the continuations with significance being compared balance at the steps before them: the level history with this part retains with respect to the level history with it withheld exactly where, for every continuation with significance admitted by the withheld levels, at every condition it depends on, the need plus this part's cumulative taking is at most the withheld level plus this part's cumulative giving (the cumulative taking and giving both counting the steps before its step);

the level history with it withheld adds with respect to the level history with this part exactly where, for some continuation with significance admitted by the withheld levels, this does not hold at every condition it depends on;

the level history with this part adds with respect to the level history with it withheld exactly where, for some continuation with significance not admitted by the withheld levels, at every condition it depends on, the need plus this part's cumulative taking is at most the withheld level plus this part's cumulative giving.
Where the flow balances everywhere, the same holds.
This holds whatever the significance.
A valuation gives together, over the claims, living, a relation among claims, own region and significance.
Living, read step by step, is a relatum active at a step and not undermined.

title_en: Living crosses recurring arising and recurring ceasing

clauses.en: Among worlds with finitely many relata, those where arising recurs and those where it does not each have instances where every event is living and instances where not every event is living;
those where ceasing recurs and those where it does not also each have these two instances.
In a world with finitely many relata in which activity is decided, ceasing recurs exactly where arising recurs (三·五).

So in worlds with finitely many relata, whether every event is living is not fixed by whether arising and ceasing recur, and whether arising and ceasing recur is not fixed by whether every event is living.
Self-significance is where every living claim in a standpoint's own region has significance from this standpoint.
A seed is where some living claim has significance from some standpoint.
Held is where every living claim lies in some standpoint's own region.
If a standpoint has self-significance and its own region has a living claim, then there is a seed.
Taking the relata as standpoints and own region as the region along any relation, read step by step, every living claim is held.

title_en: Boundary neutrality, bounded rule, relational neutrality, standpoint neutrality

clauses.en: Boundary neutrality is a rule holding in every one of its instances.
A bounded rule is a rule holding within a formed boundary.
Whatever has boundary neutrality holds within any boundary.
Relational neutrality is the boundary neutrality of the rule "a living claim related to a claim with significance from a standpoint also has significance from this standpoint".
Standpoint neutrality is the boundary neutrality of the rule "a living claim with significance from one standpoint has significance from every standpoint";
for the significance of continuation, what has significance from one standpoint having significance from every standpoint is also called standpoint neutrality.

With interacting or descent (in both directions) as the relation among claims, if there is relational neutrality (十五·九): from a standpoint, if any event of a relatum has significance, then every living event of what descends from this relatum also has significance;
if any event of a relatum has significance, then every living event of what this relatum descends from also has significance.
Living significance is where every living claim has significance from every standpoint.

title_en: The laws of the web do not imply living significance

clauses.en: For every web with a standpoint and a relatum living at a step: on this web, with the significance that holds of everything, there is living significance;
with the significance that holds of nothing, living significance does not hold, and for every two level histories the one retains with respect to the other and does not add with respect to it.
Living claims are connected where, for every two living claims, from the one, moving at each step along the relation among claims to a living claim, the other can be reached.

For every valuation with a standpoint and a living claim whose living claims are connected: there is living significance exactly where there is a seed, relational neutrality and standpoint neutrality.

Without the seed, without relational neutrality, without standpoint neutrality, or without connection, there is in each case a valuation that has the other three and in which living significance does not hold.
With "depends on or draws from one and the same condition" as the relation among claims: if every living event depends on or draws from one condition, then the living events are connected;
if moreover there are a standpoint and a living event, then there is living significance exactly where there is a seed, relational neutrality and standpoint neutrality.

With interacting as the relation among claims (二·十四): adding a condition that every relatum depends on with need zero and that nothing draws from leaves the living events unchanged; with the former relation the living events of every web are then connected, and with interacting whether they are connected is as before;

adding a condition whose level is one at every step, that every relatum depends on with need one, and that only the relatum of one living event draws from at the step of this event, this condition is renewed, the living events are unchanged, and with interacting the living events of every web are connected.

There is a web in which two formations depend on a condition with need one and are active exactly where the level of this condition is not below one, and another relatum draws from it only at the first step;
where the level of this condition is one at every step, with interacting the living events are connected;
where the level of this condition falls to zero after the first step, the events of the two formations at the first step are both living, and with interacting they are not connected;
with the former relation, both are connected.

title_en: Living significance where every living claim is held

clauses.en: For every valuation in which every living claim is held: there is living significance exactly where every standpoint has self-significance and there is standpoint neutrality;
connection is not needed, and relational neutrality is not needed.

For every valuation whose living claims are connected, where every standpoint's own region has a living claim, every standpoint has self-significance, and there is relational neutrality, there is living significance.

Taking the relata as standpoints and own region as the region along any relation, read step by step, there is living significance exactly where every relatum has self-significance and there is standpoint neutrality.

title_en: The center is not fixed by dependence

clauses.en: There is a world in which each relatum's own region is its own events, each relatum's own events have significance from it, and the events of the relatum that gives the clearer what it draws from (the source) also have significance from the clearer;

every living claim is held, there is self-significance everywhere, and for every event with significance from a standpoint, the events of what takes part at the same step and gives to a condition that the relatum of this event depends on also have significance from this standpoint;

the dweller's event at step zero is living and related to the clearer's event at step zero, and has no significance from the clearer's standpoint: standpoint neutrality does not hold, living significance does not hold, and relational neutrality restricted to claims with significance in this standpoint's own region does not hold either.
In it, the clearer's event at step one is in its own region, active and not living.

Bounded significance is where, from a standpoint, only the continuations of what lies within its region have significance: from a standpoint, a relatum's continuation has significance exactly where this relatum lies within this standpoint's region.
Bounded significance holds throughout within its region.
There is a world in which each relatum's significance stops at its region along dependence, and the level history with the clearer's part withheld exists;
then the level history with this part, from the clearer's standpoint, retains with respect to the level history with it withheld, and from the dweller's standpoint loses the dweller.

title_en: Comparison stops at what is reached

clauses.en: For every flow that balances and any part taken, the level history with this part withheld exists.

If from a standpoint two significances agree at every step on every relatum this part reached before, the one holding where the other holds and the converse: then, comparing the level history with this part and the level history with it withheld under the two significances, retains in both directions is the same, and not adding in both directions is also the same.

If, for a significance, from a standpoint, the continuation at each step of every relatum this part reached before that step has significance: then the level history with this part retains with respect to the one with it withheld exactly where it includes it;
the one with it withheld retains with respect to the one with this part exactly where it includes it;
this does not add with respect to that exactly where this does not exceed that, in both directions.

Wherever two flows both balance, what takes part is the same, the starting levels are the same, and the formations outside the part respond through their couplings: for every significance, if from a standpoint the continuation at every step of everything whose lying in the responsive reach (十一·八) cannot be refuted has significance, then one flow's level history retains with respect to the other flow's level history exactly where it includes it;
it does not add exactly where it does not exceed;
both hold in both directions.

Wherever two flows both balance, what takes part is the same, the starting levels are the same, and the formations outside the part follow in both flows one law that reads through couplings: the comparison is likewise, with no further premise of response.

title_en: What the derived range does not reach

clauses.en: What a relatum's continuation requires, derived along drawing, is its feeding closure (十一·四).
There is a world that balances and is dependent, in which a relatum depends only on one condition and is active and admitted at every step;
the relatum that draws from what it gives is inactive from step four on.
There is a world that balances and is dependent, in which a relatum is active only at step zero and step one, and is admitted whenever active;
at step two, its renewer is inactive while its successor is still active;
from step three on every relatum is inactive;
without this relatum, its renewer and its successor are active at every step.

There is a world that balances, dissipates and is dependent, in which the clearer is active and admitted at every step and depends only on its source, and the source is renewed, fed from beyond at every step, and has taking within giving at every step;
the clearer undermines at step one, and the dweller is inactive from step two on.

That, from every standpoint and at every step, the continuation of every relatum has significance is called the continuation condition: boundary neutrality applied to the significance of continuation.
This is a supposition: this account states it and does not assert it.
Every bounded significance with a region as its boundary holds within its region (十五·十七);
if some relatum lies outside some standpoint's region, the continuation condition does not hold.

title_en: The continuation condition implies living significance

clauses.en: If the continuation condition holds, then for every valuation in which each claim is read as the continuation of some relatum at some step, and a claim whose continuation has significance from a standpoint also has significance from this standpoint: there is living significance, every standpoint has self-significance, there is relational neutrality and standpoint neutrality, and where there are a living claim and a standpoint there is a seed;
connection is not used.
The step-by-step reading, the relational reading and the whole-run reading are all instances of it.

Positive relevance read from significance is the living claims that hold at a configuration (read as the continuation of some relatum at some step) whose continuation has significance from every standpoint.

If the continuation condition holds, then for any frame and any reading of living (each claim read as the continuation of some relatum at some step): positive relevance read from significance is exactly the living claims that hold at the configurations;
with it as the significance of the frame, living significance holds;
every significance of the frame under which living significance holds contains positive relevance read from significance.

title_en: The continuation condition is living significance extended to every relatum

clauses.en: For every frame whose claims are a relatum at a step and in which each claim holds at some configuration: the continuation condition holds exactly where living significance holds with every claim taken as living and with significance from every standpoint taken as the significance of the frame.
This holds for the level histories of every web, with no further supposition.

For every web whose step-by-step valuation has connected living events, with a standpoint and a living event, and where whether each event is living is decided: the continuation condition holds exactly where there is a seed, relational neutrality and standpoint neutrality, and the continuation of everything not living has significance from every standpoint.

title_en: Under the continuation condition, retains is includes

clauses.en: If the continuation condition holds, then from any standpoint: one level history retains with respect to another exactly where it includes it;
it adds exactly where it exceeds;
every standpoint judges the same.
Widens is exactly retains and adds, keeps the same is exactly retains in both directions, and mixed is exactly adds in both directions.
What retains from a standpoint also retains from this standpoint under bounded significance with any region as its boundary.

title_en: The continuation condition fixes the scope of significance and orders nothing

clauses.en: If the continuation condition holds, two mixed level histories each add with respect to the other and neither retains with respect to the other (十五·二十五): this supposition does not order a mixed comparison;
every history that another history widens loses a continuation with significance that the other history admits.

title_en: Where bounded significance meets the continuation condition

clauses.en: Bounded significance with the whole of the unfolding as its region is the continuation condition.

If the continuation condition holds, with the relata as standpoints, and a relatum's feeding closure is the whole of the unfolding, then from this relatum's standpoint, for every two level histories, whether one retains with respect to the other, judged by bounded significance with the feeding closure as boundary, is wholly the same as judged by the significance of the continuation condition.

If the flow has mutual dependence (every formation lies in the influence closure of every formation), then bounded significance with each center's influence closure as boundary is the continuation condition;
if every formation lies in the system closure of every formation, then bounded significance with each center's system closure as boundary is also the continuation condition;
with mutual feeding, so is bounded significance with each center's feeding closure as boundary;
and so where at some step every relatum takes part, depends on one condition and gives to it.

There is a world in which the level history with the clearer's part withheld exists: from the clearer's standpoint, under bounded significance with the feeding closure as boundary, the level history with this part retains with respect to the level history with it withheld;
if the continuation condition holds, from every standpoint it does not retain.
The presupposition is where, from a standpoint, the continuation at every step of everything within its boundary of a self has significance.

Along a relation every boundary of a self is allowed: the presupposition holds at some allowed boundary of a self exactly where the continuation of everything within the center's region along this relation has significance;
along the relation under which nothing is related, exactly where the center's own continuation has significance at every step;
along the relation under which every two relata are related, exactly where from this standpoint the continuation of every relatum has significance.
The presupposition holds at every allowed boundary of a self also exactly where from this standpoint the continuation of every relatum has significance.
The step of invariance is where, if the presupposition holds at one allowed boundary of a self, it holds at every allowed boundary of a self.

Along any relation, with every boundary of a self allowed: the continuation condition holds exactly where every standpoint's presupposition holds at some allowed boundary of a self and the step of invariance holds.

Where the whole of the unfolding is an allowed boundary of a self: the step of invariance holds exactly where "if the presupposition holds at some allowed boundary of a self, then from this standpoint the continuation of every relatum has significance";
where the presupposition holds at some allowed boundary of a self, the step of invariance holds exactly where from this standpoint the continuation of every relatum has significance;
if the step of invariance holds and some relatum's continuation has no significance from this standpoint, then the presupposition holds at no allowed boundary of a self.

title_en: The step of invariance and standpoint neutrality

clauses.en: Along a relation, where every relatum lies within some center's region along this relation and every standpoint's presupposition holds at some allowed boundary of a self: the step of invariance holds for every standpoint exactly where there is standpoint neutrality for the significance of continuation;
if there is standpoint neutrality, the continuation condition holds.

title_en: Each supposition is needed; the strength of the readings of the presupposition

clauses.en: There is a world, with boundaries of a self drawn along the relation the feeding closure rests on (every boundary of a self allowed), in which, with the significance that holds of nothing, the step of invariance holds for every standpoint and the continuation condition does not hold;

with bounded significance with the feeding closure as boundary, every standpoint's presupposition holds at some allowed boundary of a self, the step of invariance does not hold for the clearer's presupposition, and the continuation condition does not hold;

if each standpoint takes only its feeding closure as an allowed boundary of a self, then bounded significance with the feeding closure as boundary makes every standpoint's presupposition hold at this boundary with the step of invariance, the dweller is not within any allowed boundary of a self of the clearer, and the continuation condition still does not hold.

A standpoint's presupposition, holding at some allowed boundary of a self along the various relations, is ordered in strength as follows: if it holds along the relation under which every two relata are related, then it holds along the relation the system closure rests on;
if it holds along the relation the system closure rests on, then it holds along the relations the reach closure and the influence closure rest on;
if it holds along the relation the influence closure rests on, then it holds along the relation the feeding closure rests on;
if it holds along any relation, then it holds along the relation under which nothing is related.

title_en: What the step across standpoints forces

clauses.en: For every significance under which the continuation of each standpoint's center has significance from this standpoint at every step, with standpoint neutrality for the significance of continuation: the continuation of every center has significance from every standpoint.
A continuation has significance under every such significance exactly where its relatum is some standpoint's center.
The significance of the centers' continuations is the continuation condition exactly where every relatum is some standpoint's center (where there is a standpoint).

Along a relation, a continuation has significance under every significance that makes a standpoint's presupposition (with some relatum as center) hold at some allowed boundary of a self exactly where its relatum lies within this center's region along this relation.

title_en: Held of its own region and held of the claim

clauses.en: There is standpoint neutrality for the significance of continuation exactly where what is held from every standpoint is one and the same claim.
Held of its own region, "what lies within the center's region along this relation has significance": every standpoint's presupposition holds at some allowed boundary of a self;
there is standpoint neutrality exactly where the centers' regions along this relation are all the same;
it is the continuation condition exactly where the centers' regions along this relation are all the whole of the unfolding.
Held of the claim: what the step across standpoints forces is exactly what lies within some center's region along this relation.
The two readings give wholly the same significance exactly where whatever lies within one center's region lies within every center's region.
A weighting from every standpoint is each standpoint giving each event a natural-number weight.

If the weight does not change with the standpoint, then whether the weight is positive does not change with the standpoint either, and, over listed events, if the weighted count of one exceeds that of another from one standpoint, it does so from every standpoint.

There is a weighting with two standpoints in which whether the weight is positive does not change with the standpoint while the weight does, and the two standpoints count a mixed pair in opposite order of size.
On the level histories of a web: the continuation condition holds exactly where living significance holds with each admitted relatum at its step as a claim and every claim living (十五·二十四).
Preemption is drawing from a condition while nothing yet depends on it.
There is a flow that balances (only the active give;
only the active take, and take only from what they draw from;

dependent): what draws from it is active at the first step, its event at this step is within renewal and does not undermine, over the whole run it is consuming and not renewing, and the level history with its part withheld widens the level history;
if the continuation condition holds, then from every standpoint the level history does not retain with respect to the level history with it withheld, and the latter adds with respect to the former.

Wherever the flow balances and, within a part's own region (a region of formations whose membership is decided), the level history widens the level history with its part withheld (at every step, what in the own region the withheld levels admit the levels also admit;

at some step they admit one more): then the level history widens the level history with it withheld exactly where, at every step, for every formation outside the own region admitted by the withheld levels and every condition it depends on, the need plus the part's cumulative taking up to this step is at most the withheld level plus the part's cumulative giving;
the two histories are mixed exactly where, at some step, for some such formation, this does not hold at every condition it depends on.

If a formation outside the own region is admitted at some step by the withheld levels, its need at a condition exactly equals the withheld level, and the part has taken beyond giving at this condition up to this step: then the two histories are mixed.
